Uber, Lyft, and similar services

- Only the person named on the receipt can be reimbursed
- Verification of initial departure point required
- Digital receipts are accepted for arrival trip only

Reimbursements may take up to 2 months to process after the event.

# America250: Student Innovators Invited to Compete in National Startup Challenge

Undergraduate students are invited to apply for America’s Startup, a national pitch competition highlighting early-stage business ideas. Submit your proposal by March 31, 2026.

- published: 2026/03/05
- contact: Office of Strategic Marketing and Communications
- email: unonews@unomaha.edu

Big ideas often start in classrooms, labs, and late-night brainstorming sessions. America’s Startup is a national collegiate startup competition designed to spotlight and support student innovators at the earliest stages of building a business. Participants submit a proposal and pitch video outlining their idea. Selected teams advance through a multi-stage review process that includes a live pitch experience.

📅 Entries are due by 11:59 P.M. Eastern Time on March 31, 2026.

## Who Can Participate

America’s Startup is open to:

- U.S. students enrolled as undergraduates in accredited U.S. colleges, universities, or trade schools
- Founders working individually or in small teams
- Early-stage ideas, concepts, or ventures across industries
- Participants must be legal residents of the United States or U.S. territories and meet eligibility requirements outlined in the Official Contest Rules

-- Conference and Travel Stipend - Jack Kent Cooke Foundation

# Conference and Travel Stipend

The Cooke Conference and Travel Stipend provides Scholars with financial support to develop their academic expertise and their professional networks. Scholars are eligible to receive a stipend of up to $1,800 to cover travel and conference fees to support their career readiness.

The Cooke Conference and Travel Stipend application is now open. Scholars requesting funding to support their professional development travels from February 16 – May 31 are encouraged to apply by January 22. Apply here.

Eligibility

Timeline & Application Information

Guidelines

Resources

Only actively enrolled Cooke Undergraduate and Graduate Scholars are eligible for this funding.

Graduate Scholars may receive this stipend once during their scholarship program.

Undergraduate Scholars are eligible to receive the stipend twice during their scholarship program, if:

- the second request is in a different academic year than the first request.
- the second experience shows a progression in their career development. (Example: The first experience was to attend a conference and the second experience was to present at a conference.)

The stipend can only support travel to one event from October – May for Scholars who are actively enrolled in school at the time of their application

title: Student & Trainee Travel Award | Stanford Center for Digital Health

Student & Trainee Travel Award | Stanford Center for Digital Health

# Student & Trainee Travel Award

About: The Stanford Center for Digital Health (CDH) aims to support innovative research at the intersection of health and technology to advance digital health in a way that is scientifically rigorous and ethically sound.

CDH Student & Trainee Travel Award: The Stanford Center for Digital Health is offering awards up to $1,000 to support travel for Stanford graduate students, residents, and postdoctoral fellows giving oral presentations on topics related to digital health at scientific conferences. CDH’s goal for these awards is to support students' and trainees’ participation in academic conferences, providing them with opportunities to develop their public speaking skills, network with like-minded peers, disseminate information about their research, and continue their learning in areas that could positively affect their research.

Eligibility: To be eligible for the award, applicants must be currently enrolled at Stanford in a graduate program, residency program, fellowship program or post-doctoral program. Applicants must be accepted to give an oral presentation at a scientific meeting. Funding will be granted only upon proof of an acceptance notification to present at an academic conference. It is strongly recommended to apply at least one month before conference travel begins.

# The Office of Undergraduate Research and Major Awards

# Undergraduate Research Travel Fellowship
The Office of Undergraduate Research and Major Awards offers the Undergraduate Research
Travel Fellowship to support undergraduate students from the University of Houston
in enhancing their academic development, disseminating their research results, and
increasing the visibility of the institution by supporting undergraduate student travel
at regional, national, and international conferences. The travel funding is intended
for undergraduates presenting the results of their research or creative activities
at meetings for a regional, national, or international audience within their academic
discipline.
**The Undergraduate Research Travel Fellowship application is now closed for the 2024-2025
academic year. Please check back in August for the 2025-2026 URTF application.**
## Funding Offered
Students may apply for up to $500 to cover travel expenses associated with attending
and presenting their research or creative work at a conference.
The Undergraduate Research Travel Fellowship may not cover all expected travel expenses.
Students are strongly encouraged to seek additional funding through research grants,
conference travel award programs, and awards offered by their department

# Grants & Scholarships

 

The LLVM Foundation supports the long-term health of the LLVM Project through education, community building, and connecting students with the broader compiler ecosystem.

​

###### Student Travel Grants

Our travel grant program funds undergraduate and graduate students to attend LLVM Developers' Meetings. Grants cover conference tickets, hotel accommodation, flights, and other travel expenses.

​

###### Upcoming Grant Round

2026 EuroLLVM Developers' Meeting

Deadline: January 19, 2026

​

###### Other Conferences

We can also fund students presenting LLVM-related work at other compiler conferences. Email board@llvm.org with details about your presentation and we'll evaluate your request.

​

### LLVM Developers' Meeting Student Travel Grants FAQ

###### ​

The LLVM Foundation is committed to diversity and education in the fields of compilers and tools, and to supporting the long-term health and growth of the LLVM Project. As part of this commitment, we offer Student Travel Grants to assist full-time undergraduate and graduate students in attending the LLVM Developers' Meeting.

Eligible expenses typically include conference registration, hotel accommodation ( booked directly by the Foundation), and airfare reimbursement. Please review the FAQ below for detailed information.
